change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: A link to a machine this client can't reach now shows a live "Thread" chip instead of "Thread on another machine"
findings.body: Before this change, a thread the client didn't know rendered `UnresolvedChip` with `unknownThreadLinkLabel`. That label tells the user "Thread on another machine" when a v2 link names a different environment. Now the unresolved chip only renders when `titles.isSuccess && !titles.isPending`. For a v2 link to an environment that isn't connected, the `threadTitles` query runs against that environment (line 55). It can't succeed, so it stays Initial or turns into Failure (`EnvironmentRpcUnavailableError`, packages/client-runtime/src/state/runtime.ts:886). The chip then renders as a clickable `ThreadContextChip` titled "Thread" with the "Open thread" tooltip, and it navigates to a route that can't load. An older server without `getThreadTitles` hits the same failure, so every unknown link looks openable. Keeping transient failures clickable is fine. But when `props.link.environmentId` differs from `props.environmentId` and isn't connected, fall back to the existing `unknownThreadLinkLabel` chip rather than a fake "Thread" link.

findings.title: Placeholder "Thread" title stops v1 links from being matched to another environment while loading or after a failure
findings.body: `threadTitleAtom` now returns "Thread" (never null) whenever the `threadTitles` query hasn't succeeded. `resolveThreadLink` (lines 236-242) treats any non-null title as proof the thread exists. So for a v1 link, the written candidate in the message's environment wins whenever the query is Initial or failed. `guessThreadLinkRef`, which would find the thread in the other connected environment it actually lives in, is never reached. The same thing happens when the percent-decoded candidate is the real one: the written candidate wins first. A tap in ThreadFeed (`apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadFeed.tsx:2853`) then opens the wrong environment's thread. Chip icons (line 146) resolve against the wrong ref too. If the RPC keeps failing (an older server, or the environment offline), this stays wrong for the session. Only a settled success with no title returns null and lets the guess run. Consider keeping the placeholder in the label path only, and having `resolveThreadLink` require a real shell or successful title.

findings.title: Deleted threads in message and composer chips now say "Open thread"
findings.body: Dropping the `shell ? … : "Thread no longer available"` branch also affects the other callers: `UserMessageContextChips.tsx:321` and `composerContextPresentation.tsx:337`. Those callers never run a title lookup. For them, a missing shell used to show "no longer available", and it now promises "Open thread" for threads that really were deleted. The Markdown path now decides availability itself, but these two callers have no replacement signal. You could pass availability in as a prop, or run the same title lookup there.

findings.title: One `getThreadTitles` RPC per unloaded link, with no caching
findings.body: Each `UnloadedThreadLink` issues its own query, keyed by its own one- or two-id input. The family has `staleTimeMs: 0, idleTtlMs: 0` (packages/client-runtime/src/state/orchestration.ts:54-55), so it refetches on every remount, e.g. when virtualized message rows scroll back into view. Mobile does the same per ref (`apps/mobile/src/state/entities.ts:66`), even though `threadLinkRefs` already collects every ref in a message. A message with many links to older threads sends one round trip per link. Batching per message, as `useLiveThreadLinkLabels` already groups refs, would make it one.

findings.title: `!== undefined` on the titles record matches prototype keys
findings.body: The sibling caller uses `Object.hasOwn(resolvedThreadTitles, threadId)` (ThreadRelationshipsControl.tsx:538). Here `titles.data?.[ref.threadId] !== undefined` holds for an id like `constructor`, and line 68 then calls `.trim` on a Function and throws. Link ids come from agent-written Markdown, so using `Object.hasOwn` would match the sibling and remove the edge case.

contracts.action: Unloaded Markdown thread link looks up its title through orchestrationEnvironment.threadTitles
contracts.before_after: The sibling skips the query when there are no ids and treats only a settled success without the key as gone (Object.hasOwn). The new path uses `!== undefined` and keeps the chip clickable on failure.
contracts.visible_effect: The chip shows "Thread" while loading or on failure, the resolved title on success, and "Thread no longer available" after an empty success.
contracts.failure_mode: On failure, or for an unreachable environment, it stays a clickable "Thread" chip with no error. A v2 link to another machine no longer says "Thread on another machine".

contracts.action: Mobile threadTitleAtom falls back to the threadTitles query when there is no shell
contracts.equivalent_path: resolveThreadLink plus guessThreadLinkRef for v1 links
contracts.before_after: Before, null meant unknown and triggered the cross-environment guess. Now a non-success query returns "Thread", which counts as known.
contracts.visible_effect: The link label becomes "Thread"; tapping it opens the message-environment ref.
contracts.failure_mode: If the RPC fails, the wrong environment is picked for the rest of the session.

summary:
I reviewed all four files and found two likely bugs, both medium confidence. Both come from treating a failed or still-loading `threadTitles` lookup as if the thread exists.

**Bugs (fix):**
- **Web:** a link to a machine this client can't reach used to show "Thread on another machine". Now it shows a clickable "Thread" chip with an "Open thread" tooltip, pointing at a thread that can't load.
- **Mobile:** while the lookup is loading or after it fails, the placeholder "Thread" title counts as a match. That skips the step that finds a v1 link's thread in another connected environment, so tapping the link opens the wrong one.

**Worth considering:**
- Removing the tooltip branch in `ThreadContextChip` changes two other callers, the message chips and the composer chips. Truly deleted threads there now say "Open thread".
- Each unloaded link sends its own lookup with no caching. A message with many links to older threads means one round trip per link.
- The web title check uses `!== undefined` where the existing sibling uses `Object.hasOwn`. A thread id like `constructor` would make it throw.

The new browser test covers loading, failure, success and empty results. It mocks the entity hooks, so it doesn't exercise the case of a link to another machine.
